summary: Full E2E backend test of the NEW Syndication / Investor Portal module (26 endpoints) on Railway prod + re-verification of OCR fix. 31 pytest cases executed: 27 PASSED, 4 FAILED. ALL 4 failures share ONE root cause: the investor portal data endpoints crash with 500 because they reference `user['id']` while `auth_marketplace()` returns the dict from `serialize()` which only has `_id` (no `id` alias). PART 1 RESULTS — Deals CRUD ✅ all 6 pass (create, list w/ auth gate, get, patch, public list, public slug detail). Investments / Cap Table ✅ all 3 pass with pro-rata equity recompute exactly correct (100% → 66.67/33.33 → 80/20). Distributions ✅ all 3 pass with pro-rata payouts (8000/2000 on 80/20 split, exact), paid-state propagation to total_distributions_received works, and DELETE on paid dist correctly returns 400. Documents ✅ both pass (upload returns metadata without base64 data, GET deal includes doc list). Investors directory ✅ all 3 pass (list, detail, reset-password returns temp). Investor auth ✅ both pass (wrong-pw → 401, correct-pw → JWT with role=investor). Investor scoped data ❌ 3 of 3 FAIL with 500 (dashboard, list-my-deals, deal-detail-with-403-check). Public inquiry ✅ passes. Cleanup ✅ all 4 deletes pass. PART 2 — OCR ✅ /api/tenant/utilities/scan now returns 200 (no longer 500 'No hay API key configurada'). Railway EMERGENT_LLM_KEY env var fix is verified.

critical.issue: CRITICAL: All 6 investor portal data routes are broken (HTTP 500). Root cause: they call `ObjectId(user['id'])` but `auth_investor` -> `auth_marketplace` -> `serialize(user)` returns a dict whose user id key is `_id` (string), NOT `id`. So `user['id']` raises KeyError -> FastAPI 500. Fix: change all 6 occurrences in syndication_router.py to `user['_id']` (already string-serialized) — lines 994, 1013, 1042, 1062, 1078, 1129, 1163. Alternatively, modify `auth_marketplace` (rental/shared.py) to also set `user['id'] = user['_id']` so any caller can use either key. Confirmed via grep — these are the only 6 `user["id"]` references in the syndication router. The investor /login and /change-password old_password verification work fine since they use `user['_id']` from a fresh DB lookup; only the auth-context propagation is broken.

minor.issue: Response returns `equity_percent: 0` in the synchronous response body because `_recompute_deal_totals()` runs AFTER the in-memory object was already built for the response. The persisted DB value is correct (verified via subsequent GET). Cosmetic only — fix: re-fetch the investment from DB after recompute before serializing the response.

The slug for 'Test Deal QA' was 'test-deal-qa' (auto-generated by _slugify), not 'banking-filter-hub' as the review request suggested. Not a bug, just a doc/typo in the request — the endpoint works correctly with the actual generated slug.

Also line 1042 uses it inside the dashboard response payload. After the fix re-run pytest /app/backend/tests/test_syndication_e2e.py — expect 31/31 pass.

Re-deploy to Railway after the fix — the test target is prod, so local-only fixes won't change test outcome until deployed.

syndication_router.py:228 — `_parse_date` is defined AFTER it's first referenced (at line 213, inside the create_deal dict literal). Works in Python because the dict is only evaluated when create_deal is called, but it's confusing — move the helper above the route.

rca_of_issue: Bug RCA — Investor portal 500s: `rental/shared.py:serialize()` returns a dict where the primary key is `_id` (stringified ObjectId). It does NOT add an `id` alias. `auth_marketplace` returns `serialize(user)` directly. `auth_investor` (syndication_router.py:59) just wraps `auth_marketplace` and returns the same dict. But every investor data route then does `ObjectId(user['id'])`, which throws KeyError → FastAPI converts to 500 Internal Server Error. Reproduction: (1) admin creates deal + investment for qa.investor1@test.com (auto-creates app_users row with role=investor), (2) admin POSTs /api/admin/syndication/investors/{id}/reset-password to get temp pw, (3) POST /api/investor/login → 200 + JWT, (4) GET /api/investor/dashboard with that JWT → 500 'Internal Server Error'. Mitigation (one of): (a) replace `user['id']` with `user['_id']` everywhere in syndication_router.py investor routes (6 occurrences), OR (b) add `user['id'] = user['_id']` alias in shared.py:serialize() so consumers can use either key. Option (b) is safer (works for any future caller) but (a) is the minimal fix. Note: investor LOGIN works fine because that endpoint queries DB directly and uses `user['_id']` itself — it's only the auth context propagation to downstream routes that's broken.
